title: adaptive-kernel-selection-kvcache-experiment-log
content:
Summary:

This is the working log for a concentrated experimental pass combining adaptive kernel selection, scheduler heuristics, and KV-cache policy tweaks. Goal: find configurations that reduce 95th-percentile token latency while preserving throughput (tokens/s) and lowering per-token GPU compute cost for medium-length chat workloads (avg request length 256 tokens, context 1024). This doc captures microbench setups, trace-driven replay results, unexpected regressions, and immediate action items.

Background and motivation:
- Prior runs showed kernel A (fp16 fused attention) is fastest for short sequences but regresses when KV-cache hit rate falls below ~70% due to kernel warmup and higher register pressure. Kernel B (mixed-quant int8) has better steady-state throughput on long sequences but higher cold-start latency.
- Scheduler currently picks kernel by static rules: sequence_length_threshold + model_family. We want an adaptive selector that uses recent trace-level metrics (mm_latency, cache_hit_rate, recent_batch_size) to choose per-request kernels and schedule placement (dedicated vs shared GPU pool).

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Variables: kernel_variant {A, B, C}, kv_cache_policy {aggressive_evict, lru, prefix_only}, scheduler_mode {static, short-path-adaptive, trace-window-adaptive}, batch_window_ms {2, 8, 20}.
- Workloads: chat-medium (avg 256 tokens), longform (avg 1024 tokens), search-rerank (short queries with many parallel requests).
- Baselines: production static kernel selection (prod-config-2026-01).

Microbench setup and harness notes:
- Executor: local 4x A100-40GB emulated cluster; each run binds to a single GPU for consistent KV metrics.
- Replayer: use trace-replay v2 (use-case tag: chat-medium) with synthetic inter-arrival jitter (~exp with mean 50ms). Trace seeds: TR-2025-11-08-CHT-01..04.
- Measurement: per-request metrics emitted to bench collector: request_id, seq_len, kv_hit_percent, kernel_chosen, token_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), tokens_generated, gpu_compute_ms, batch_size_at_send.
- Warmup: 3 minutes per config, then 5 minutes measurement. Each config repeated 3 times; median taken.
- Important commands: 
  - replay: ./tools/trace_replay --trace TR-2025-11-08-CHT-01 --jitter 50 --duration 8m --out bench_run_X.json
  - kernel toggle: ./runtime/bin/kernel_ctl --set-policy adaptive-window --window-ms 20

Key results (selected, median across runs):
- Baseline (static): chat-medium p95 token latency = 48ms, throughput = 85k tokens/s, kv_hit = 72%, cost_estimated_cpu/gpu = base.
- Adaptive short-path-adaptive + kernel A/B hybrid + lru kv: p95 = 36ms (-25%), throughput = 92k tokens/s (+8%), kv_hit = 75% (+3%). Notable: p99 still spikes to 210ms in 1/3 runs correlated with eviction storms.
- Trace-window-adaptive (window=20ms) + kernel B preferred for sequences >480 tokens + prefix_only cache policy: p95 = 42ms (-12%), throughput = 110k tokens/s (+29%), kv_hit = 68% (-4%). Lower hit-rate but much better throughput for longform.
- Aggressive_evict + kernel C (quant-int8 opt) under short-path scheduling produced lower cost per token (-18%) but p95 regressions for chat-medium (p95 = 56ms, worse than baseline).

Observed regressions and root-cause hypotheses:
1) p99 spikes in short-path-adaptive runs: correlated with concurrent eviction events on the same shard. Hypothesis: adaptive policy sometimes reduces retention window in response to observed low reuse, then immediately sees reuse due to conversational turns landing on other requests — thrashing.
   - Evidence: trace timeline shows eviction markers followed by high kv_cache_miss percentages within 200ms.
   - Mitigation idea: introduce randomized retention jitter per shard and minimum retention TTL of 800ms.

2) Cold-start kernel latency on Kernel B after autoscaling: when new worker spins up, kernel selection logic prefers kernel B but code path triggers expensive kernel compilation on first request. Hypothesis: lazy JIT triggers synchronous compilation blocking request processing.
   - Evidence: logs show compile_ms ~ 450ms on first request, subsequent requests fine.
   - Mitigation idea: pre-warm kernels during scale-up with async compilation; fall back to kernel A during worker warm-up.

3) Cost vs latency tradeoff for prefix_only policy: trading cache space for throughput reduces average per-token GPU compute but increases p95 on chat workloads when many short requests rely on prefix matches.
   - Evidence: synthetic reruns with higher short request proportion show p95 increased by 20% for prefix_only.
   - Mitigation idea: dynamic hybrid: prefix_only for long-request-heavy buckets; lru for chat-heavy buckets. Use simple bucketization by recent avg seq_len.

Trace analysis notes (examples):
- Example trace snippet (timestamps relative):
  t=12.24s request R-452 seq=192 kernel=A kv_hit=0.85 token_latency_p95=34ms
  t=12.40s request R-453 seq=64 kernel=A kv_hit=0.12 token_latency_p95=120ms (eviction observed 12.39s)
- Root pattern: eviction storms often align with batched writes from background compaction + high churn clients. Need isolation between background jobs and real-time inference shards.

Regression checklist (actionable):
- [ ] Add retention_min_ttl config (default 800ms) and rerun short-path-adaptive. Owner: Rafael. Due: 2026-03-17.
- [ ] Implement async kernel precompile on scale-up (PR prototype exists, see linked PR 842). Owner: Maya. Due: 2026-03-24.
- [ ] Add per-shard jitter to eviction schedule to reduce synchronized eviction. Owner: Ethan. Due: 2026-03-20.
- [ ] Run mixed workload sweep (50% chat-medium, 50% longform) and collect p95/p99 baseline comparison. Owner: Aisha. Due: 2026-03-26.

Notes on instrumentation improvements:
- Need a lightweight event that flags 'eviction-cause' (compaction, memory-pressure, manual) in traces so we can attribute misses. Minimal change: add one extra log field in KV layer emitted only in bench builds.
- Add histogram buckets for kernel compilation latency (0-10ms, 10-50ms, 50-200ms, >200ms). Current metric is too coarse.

Configuration snippets (for reproducibility):
- adaptive config example:
  kernel_selector: adaptive_window
  window_ms: 20
  retention_policy: lru
  retention_min_ttl_ms: 800
  precompile_on_scaleup: true

Commands used for cost estimation:
- token cost simulated via sample-run: ./tools/cost_estimator --gpu-type a100-40 --profile bench_run_X.json --model flan-med --quant int8

Open questions and experimental forks to try next:
- Is it worthwhile to route short-chat requests to a small pool of warm workers pinned to kernel A to eliminate kernel choice latency entirely? Cost trade must be evaluated.
- Can we implement micro-batching opportunistically with deadline hints to reduce kernel-switch overhead? Example: if deadline_ms > 50ms allow 4ms extra batching delay.
- Explore cross-shard eviction coordination versus per-shard randomized TTL; which yields fewer unexpected misses under bursty traffic?

Appendix: artifact list and quick references:
- PRs: 842 (adaptive selector prototype), 858 (kv-cache retention TTL), 884 (trace-replay v2 improvements).
- Jira: RINF-7123 (adaptive selector task), RINF-7241 (kv cache eviction jitter), RINF-7310 (kernel precompile on scale-up).
- Related slack threads: #runtime-kernel-experiments (thread ts 1704000000), #perf-regressions (ref 1704105000).

Immediate next steps (this week):
1) Rafael to land TTL patch and run 3x short-path-adaptive sweeps against chat-medium traces.
2) Maya to finish async precompile prototype; run scale-up smoke tests.
3) Ethan to implement per-shard eviction jitter and include eviction-cause flag.
4) Aisha to run mixed workload cost/latency comparison and produce short memo for product (impact vs SLA).

End of log.

Notes-to-self: capture one failing p99 trace and attach to RINF-7123 for oncall investigating 'eviction storm' alerts.
